Cost optimization extends beyond technical system design and operation into considerations of electricity price structures, incentive programs, and policy initiatives, all of which can require expertise to navigate. The choice of electricity price structures, especially those that include incentive mechanisms such as peak demand charges or time-of-use (TOU) pricing, can have a significant impact on usage costs, as we show in the case studies (Section 4). In areas with high rates of EV adoption, price structures have been designed specifically to facilitate and incentivize low-grid-impact EV charging.39,40 Adapting EV fleet operations to take advantage of these structures can realize cost reductions. Many electricity providers additionally offer deliberate incentives to charge EVs in a way that lessens grid impact, such as demand response programs. Federal, state, and local governments, in addition to electricity providers, also offer a diverse set of incentives to adopt and install EVSE. The availability of these programs varies over time and by location. Many EV users may lack the expertise, interest, or time needed to take advantage of cost savings opportunities available via tariff selection, incentive programs, or policy initiatives41. A ChaaS provider can offer this expertise, and potentially even exert leverage on behalf of their customers to enhance existing opportunities or drive additional opportunities. EVSE can also be used to generate revenue, which a ChaaS provider can enable or facilitate. Revenue opportunities might include selling charging to secondary customers, selling services to the electric grid, actualizing regulatory incentives, and attracting customers for other business. When EVSE are not being used to serve the charging needs of the site host (primary customer), EVSE usage can be sold to secondary customers. EVSE and EVs can also be used to participate in electricity markets, such as providing ancillary services to the grid. The flexibility to provide such services can be enhanced by deploying vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities. There also exist policy- driven markets, such as the market for low-carbon fuel standard (LCFS) credits in California42.
